findings.evidence: Section 2 'Readiness' holds five separate procedures: the readiness test and dated pause, the urgent-matter exception ('the raise-it-now exception below covers only operational incidents'), the repair after getting defensive, reference-loading rules, and pre-weekend support. Each one is good, but the process pattern blurs here because the 'below' cross-reference points inside the same paragraph.
findings.fix: Keep every rule and split Section 2 into short labelled steps (Readiness test, Urgent exceptions, Repair after defensiveness, Before a weekend or absence). Rewrite 'the raise-it-now exception below' to name the sentence it means, e.g. 'the next sentence's exception'.

findings.evidence: "files": ["evals/files/runbook-dispute-notes.md", "references/facilitation.md"]. Several evals (facilitated-conflicting-accounts, sensitive-health-disclosure, buy-time-return-to-point, followup-check-in-peer-conflict, quick-prep-ten-minutes, pause-twenty-minutes-or-tomorrow, pre-meeting-breathing) list the skill's own reference files as input files. The without-skill baseline then gets the skill's content too, which hides the skill's delta.
findings.fix: Keep only real user inputs (such as evals/files/runbook-dispute-notes.md) in each eval's files list, and remove the references/*.md entries. Test whether the skill loads the right reference with an assertion instead, e.g. 'The session plan uses an agreed column and a disputed column, with no third column'.

findings.evidence: 'if you need longer, ask for a break with a named time (SKILL.md Section 2: "come back to you by [day]")'. SKILL.md Section 2 does not contain that line; its wording is 'fix a specific reconvening time ("Thursday 10:00")'. The quoted line is in emotional-regulation.md, in the 'I go blank when I'm criticized' row.
findings.fix: Change the parenthetical to '(SKILL.md Section 2: fix a specific reconvening time, e.g. "Thursday 10:00"; or the "come back to you by [day]" line in emotional-regulation.md)' so the cited source holds the quoted words.
